_doc: The parts list under the truck drawing on the front page (truck.svg). n matches the drawing's callout. kind: added (built or fitted for this project) or factory. Every line is a fact from the private as-built record, rewritten under public/AGENTS.md's Boundary; update it when the truck changes. hardware, software, since: the spec table on the front page. page: the part's own page, site/truck/<page>.html. status: the front page's status line, [label, HTML].

parts.name: Cameras
parts.text: An ELP AR0234 on an 8 mm lens for the narrow view and an Arducam IMX662 for the wide view, in one case on the sun-visor mount. Both are recorded on every drive.
parts.hardware: ELP AR0234 on an 8 mm lens; Arducam B0576 IMX662
parts.software: MJPEG, 20 fps recorded; one case on the sun-visor mount

parts.name: Tablet
parts.text: A Galaxy Tab Active5 Pro in the cabin running a dashboard written for this truck, with a voice assistant. It shows the decoded vehicle state and the driving model's path.
parts.software: dashboard v139, Kotlin and Compose; voice assistant

parts.name: Gateway, Raspberry Pi 5
parts.text: A Rust service that records every frame on both CAN buses from key-in to key-out and decodes 62 signals live for the tablet and the driving model.
parts.software: Rust gateway; 62 signals decoded live; every frame on both buses

parts.name: Jetson Orin NX 16 GB
parts.text: Runs comma's N16 driving model (406M parameters) with TensorRT at 20 Hz on the truck's cameras, with YOLO26s for objects and SegFormer-B0 for free ground beside it.
parts.hardware: Jetson Orin NX 16 GB, 2 TB NVMe
parts.software: N16, TensorRT fp16, 32.5 ms a step; YOLO26s at 10 Hz; SegFormer-B0 at 5 Hz

parts.name: Compute battery
parts.text: A 314 Ah LiFePO4 battery in the trunk, charged from the starting battery through a Victron Orion-Tr 12/12-30A DC-DC charger. The gateway reads both over Bluetooth.
parts.hardware: Eco-Worthy 314 Ah LiFePO4, 4,019 Wh; Victron Orion-Tr 12/12-30A
parts.software: battery and charger read over Bluetooth every 10 s

parts.name: Engine ECU, Bosch ME 2.8.1
parts.text: The controller of the M113K supercharged 5.4 L V8. Since 3 Nov 2026 it runs patched firmware that accepts a torque request on CAN at 50 Hz with a 100 ms watchdog. The patch was run on an emulator of the ECU before it was written over K-line.
parts.hardware: Bosch ME 2.8.1, Infineon C167, 512 KB flash
parts.software: stock code and calibration; torque request at 50 Hz, 100 ms watchdog; 10 Hz telemetry

parts.name: Transmission, 722.6 five-speed
parts.text: Controlled by Ultimate-NAG52, the open-source replacement for the factory EGS52, on a firmware build with five G55 patches (since 18 Oct 2026).
parts.software: firmware V15: upstream dev with 5 G55 patches; live data at 10 Hz

parts.name: Cruise control stalk
parts.text: Since 29 Oct 2026 the gateway presses the factory cruise control over CAN-C, on a command from the tablet.
parts.hardware: factory stalk on the steering-column module
parts.software: the gateway's cruise controller; SET+ accepted 7 of 7

parts.name: Steering
parts.text: Hydraulic, with no electric motor. Nothing steers the truck yet: steering is tested and trained in a simulator built from the truck's own drives.
parts.hardware: factory hydraulic steering box, no motor

parts.name: CAN buses
parts.text: CAN-C at 500 kbit/s for powertrain and chassis, CAN-B at 83.3 kbit/s for the body. 131 signals in 47 messages are decoded in the project's DBC files.
parts.software: 131 signals in 47 messages in the DBC files; 62 decoded live

status: torque request at 50 Hz, checked key on, engine off
